plan: With 3 bidders and this mechanism functioning as a second-price auction (since the clock auction with sealed exit bids results in the winner paying the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the others' bids, paying only the second-highest bid, which maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing profitable opportunities.

Since the sealed bid acts as my automatic exit price in an ascending clock auction, this mimics a second-price auction structure: I win only if my bid is highest, and I pay the second-highest bid. The dominant strategy in such mechanisms is to bid my true value, as this ensures I win whenever the price is below my value (profitable) and avoid winning when it's above my value (unprofitable). Bidding above value risks overpaying; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Thus, bidding exactly $9 is optimal.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the ascending clock ends when the second-highest sealed bid is reached, and the winner pays that price), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $34.
